hyps.why: Raising an already large learning rate causes unstable training and accuracy collapse.
Lowering an overly large learning rate restores stable convergence.
Deeper nets are more prone to divergence at high learning rates.
Shallower nets are more stable when the learning rate is high.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise, which helps when the learning rate is high.
Smaller batches add noise that compounds instability at high learning rates.
Wider layers give more capacity and smoother optimization at high learning rates.
Strong L2 regularization further increased causes underfitting.
Relaxing very strong L2 regularization reduces underfitting.
With a tiny learning rate the net is undertrained in 243 epochs, so raising it helps.
